previous_statement: Precisely, substituting B_{P_n,Q_n}=iota_n(B_{P,Q}) from 1.2 into the defining formula gives only Co_{P_n,Q_n}=theta(iota_n(B_{P,Q})). The desired right-hand side is iota_n(theta(B_{P,Q})); no algebraic manipulation of the defining formula identifies them. The missing equation is exactly the conditional conclusion of 1.3, whose extra functional-calculus hypothesis is absent. Thus the verifier objection identifies a genuine missing allowed premise rather than a bridgeable proof gap.
new_statement: The missing amplification equation is not derivable from the registered inputs, independently of node 1.3. Indeed, with A=C direct-sum C, 0<s<=1/2, P=Q=(1-s,s), and delta=s-s^2, the raw compression is R(x,y)=((1-s)^2 x,s^2 y). The explicitly stated properties of def-compressed-corner are simultaneously satisfied at level one by E(x,y)=(x,0) and at level two (identifying M_2 tensor A with M_2 direct-sum M_2) by F(X,Y)=(X+delta Y,0): both maps are idempotent, involution-preserving, and universally O(delta)-close to the corresponding raw compression. But F is not iota_2(E), since iota_2(E)(X,Y)=(X,0). Because the registered definition imposes no relation between the otherwise unspecified theta-corrections at different matrix levels, it permits theta(B_{P,Q})=E and theta(B_{P_2,Q_2})=F. Hence Co_{P_2,Q_2}=iota_2(Co_{P,Q}) is not a consequence of the allowed statements; amplification naturality (or a fixed natural functional calculus) is an additional premise.
